title: Reset Sprint Catalyst Notebook
content:
Purpose:
- Short scratchpad for a quick quarter-reset + two-week sprint plan for my personal OKRs and day-to-day cadence. Not a polished doc — actionable bullets and questions to bring to 1:1.

Top-level objective (Q2 personal):
- Reduce recurring context-switch cost and raise weekly deep-work output by 30% while keeping on-call handover latency <= 15 mins.

KR draft (tracked weekly):
- KR1: Average deep-focus blocks (>=90 uninterrupted minutes) = 6/week -> baseline (current) = 3.
- KR2: PR throughput (merged PRs that touch runtime perf or infra) = 4/month -> baseline = 2.
- KR3: On-call handover checklists automated -> 100% of shifts have checklist link in PagerDuty incident notes (current ~60%).

Why these? quick rationale:
- Focus blocks correlate with meaningful perf work (benchmarks, profiling).
- PR throughput nudges me to ship more smaller improvements vs long unreviewed forks.
- Handover reliability reduces context-switching overhead for rest of team.

Monthly metrics snapshot (me):
- Feb merged PRs: 1 (perf refactor)
- Jan deep-focus blocks/week avg: 2.8
- Handover checklist coverage: ~58%

Two-week sprint commitments (next sprint):
- Ship: (1) KV-cache eviction tweak + regression test suite (ENG-1982) -> target PR by Fri 2026-03-12.
- Measure: add per-route cold-start histogram to perf dashboard (console route) -> dashboard card + alert.
- Automate: make handover checklist a template in PagerDuty, add link to /ops/handover-checklist.md.
- Personal: schedule 6x90m deep work slots across two weeks (block calendar, do not accept meetings during those slots).

Hypotheses & experiments:
- H1: If I block 90-minute sessions and protect them, I will complete at least 50% more measurable perf work per sprint.
  - Experiment: Bicycle cadence — assign two morning blocks per week for profiling, two afternoon for PR polish.
- H2: Small, frequent PRs reduce review time and increase throughput vs one large PR.
  - Experiment: split big refactor into three incremental PRs, measure time-to-merge and review comments.

Weekly check-in template (to copy into weekly notes):
- Wins: quick bullets.
- Metrics: deep blocks, PRs merged, checklist coverage.
- Blockers: what needs help (people/tickets).
- Next week: 3 MITs (most important tasks).

Retrospective (last sprint) — raw notes:
- What went well:
  - Finished a diagnostic harness for KV-cache (faster iteration).
  - Pair review with Ravi sped up review and reduced rework.
- What didn't:
  - Meetings bled into focus windows (two unexpected syncs).
  - Forgot to add handover checklist link twice -> incident on Sat night that cost follow-up time.
- Actions taken:
  - Set calendar guard rails and added "do not book unless urgent" note on blocks.
  - Drafted PagerDuty template (needs templating permissions).

Open questions / blockers to raise in 1:1:
- Need 30m of support from Platform Eng to add the per-route cold-start metric to the global dashboard (who owns grafana queries?). Ticket: ENG-2389 (raised but awaiting triage).
- Can SRE grant me permission to add the PagerDuty template? Who is the contact? (cc: @Avery Lin in Slack).

Tactical TODOs (priority-ordered):
- [ ] Split perf refactor into 3 PRs (create branches + outline).
- [ ] Push KV-cache regression tests and run CI profiles.
- [ ] Open a small PR for dashboard card with placeholder metric (so it exists).
- [ ] Follow up with SRE about PD template permission (email).
- [ ] Block calendar for 6x90m slots for next two weeks.

Notes to self: (unfiltered)
- Keep PR scope tight. If it grows, make a follow-up PR.
- When pairing, nominate a reviewer before starting to code.
- If an on-call incident hits during a deep block, try to triage in 15 mins, then signal to re-schedule the rest of the block.

Quick links / tickets to copy into meeting:
- ENG-1982 (KV-cache eviction tweak)
- ENG-2389 (dashboard metric ownership)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/742 (perf harness)
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/2026+Q2+Planning

Reflection cues for end-of-week journal:
- Did I protect my blocks? If not, why?
- What small win moved the needle?
- What is one cleanup action to make next week easier?

Last line (commitment):
- This sprint: ship one measurable perf improvement, make handover frictionless, protect focused time. Small consistent progress > occasional big swings.

(end)
